main_text.p: à quibus scatet fæcibus repurgarent, ut contaminatiorem multo nobis exhiberent, sanioribus expunctis sequiora inseruerunt[?]; quæque verso stylo D. Bucerus eximiæ pietatis & reconditæ eruditionis Theologus olim delevit, ea repofuerunt; adeo ut nullus sit in farraginea[?] pontificiorum errorum mole cuius in ea fere maturam messem aut fermentem saltem oculatus & judiciosus lector non deprehendet. Hinc novorum motuum & tot malorum origo quæ exterorum aures[?] atque animos implevit. Nam cum Regio diplomate in eas angustias Pastores & populus conjecti essent, ut vel perduellionis crimen subire vel illam liturgiam contra jusjurandum, fidem, Ecclesiæ & Patriæ instituta amplecti cogerentur, effectum est, ut Regni omnes Ordines quorum jamdudum in tolerandis Episcopis patientia obrutuit, hujus liturgiæ experrecti nuncio de profligandis corruptelis & primæva puritate restituenda consilium inierint. Regem itaque Serenissimum complurimis supplicibus libellis & sanctiorem ejus Senatum rogare, orare, hortari non destiterunt, ut afflictæ Ecclesiæ succurrerent, in Episcopos vero tantorum malorum authores serio animadverterent. Dum tardius auxilium parari, supplicibus libellis non responderi, postulata sua nihil pensi haberi cernerent; in se altius descendunt, mentis latebras penitus excutiunt, violati fœderis memoria conscientias pungit, lancinat, perfodit; quare seria pœnitentia ducti fœdus cum fidei confessione renovare statuerunt; quæ Chiro-graphis primo consignarunt, deinde solenni indicto jejunio jurejurando sublatis dexteris multo cum gemitu & lachrymis publice in templis confirmarunt. Dum hæc aguntur missus est à Serenissimo Rege Marchio Hamiltonius ad controversias has cognoscendas, lites componendas & tempestates omnes in tranquillum redigendas: cujus ope & industria hoc confe-

page.notes: Long s rendered as plain s throughout. Uncertain readings: "sequiora inseruerunt" (ink blur over the word that could be read differently), "farraginea" (the final letters are obscured by a stain), "aures" (the word after "exterorum" is partly cut by a fold, so the reading is a guess). The word "salutem" is broken at the line end as "sal-/tem" and is read as "saltem", since it fits the sense. The page has no printed page number. No marginal notes are printed.
